items.q: A 5-year-old has golden-yellow crusted erosions around the mouth and nose that spread peripherally. The most likely diagnosis is?
items.exp: Non-bullous impetigo presents with honey-coloured crusts on erosions at the face and nares, caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes.
r: Incorrect. That gives grouped vesicles on red base.
Incorrect. That gives dry lichenified flexural patches.
Incorrect. That gives annular scaly rings.
Correct. Honey crusts at the oral-nasal area.
items.kp: Honey crusts around nose mean impetigo.

items.q: A toddler develops flaccid blisters that rupture into moist red areas with radial crusting but no scarring. The toxin mechanism is?
o: Staphylococcal exfoliative toxin splitting the granular layer
items.exp: Bullous impetigo and scalded skin arise from exfoliative toxins A or B cleaving desmoglein-1 in the superficial epidermis.
r: Incorrect. That causes ecthyma gangrenosum necrosis.
Incorrect. That causes pseudomembranes.
Correct. Exfoliative toxin gives superficial split.
Incorrect. That causes scarlet-fever rash.
items.kp: Fragile blisters in children mean exfoliative toxin.

items.q: An ulcerated crusted lesion on the shin with an adherent crust that leaves a punched-out ulcer is?
items.exp: Ecthyma is a deeper ulcerative form of impetigo with adherent crust over a punched-out ulcer, common on shins.
r: Incorrect. That has painless black eschar with oedema.
Correct. Adherent crust over punched-out ulcer.
Incorrect. That is necrotic with black eschar in neutropenia.
Incorrect. That has undermined violaceous borders.
items.kp: Adherent crust over ulcer means ecthyma.

items.q: A rapidly spreading hot red swollen leg with a sharply raised advancing edge and fever best fits?
items.exp: Erysipelas involves superficial dermis and lymphatics with a well-demarcated raised edge, usually streptococcal, with systemic features.
r: Correct. Raised sharp border with fever.
Incorrect. Cellulitis has a diffuse flat border.
Incorrect. That has severe pain, bullae and toxicity.
Incorrect. That gives tender shin nodules without heat spread.
items.kp: Raised sharp edge with fever is erysipelas.

items.q: A febrile 2-year-old has generalised tender red skin with sheets peeling around the mouth, sparing the mucosae. The diagnosis is?
items.exp: Scalded skin shows superficial Nikolsky-positive peeling with mucosal sparing in small children from exfoliative toxin.
r: Incorrect. That involves mucosae with full-thickness necrosis.
Incorrect. That adds conjunctivitis, lymph nodes and oedema.
Incorrect. That has sandpaper rash plus strawberry tongue.
Correct. Superficial peel with spared mucosae in a toddler.
items.kp: Peeling child with spared mucosae is scalded skin.

items.q: A diabetic man has a painful deep nodule on the nape coalescing with discharging sinuses. This carbuncle differs from a furuncle by?
o: Coalescent follicular abscesses with multiple openings
Single hair-follicle abscess with one core
items.exp: A carbuncle is a coalescence of adjacent furuncles with multiple draining points, common on the nape in diabetics.
r: Incorrect. Carbuncles are follicular in origin.
Incorrect. That describes hidradenitis.
Correct. Multiple openings mark carbuncle.
Incorrect. That describes a single furuncle.
items.kp: Many openings on nape means carbuncle.

items.q: A neutropenic patient develops a rapidly enlarging necrotic ulcer with a black centre and red halo in the groin. The likely organism is?
items.exp: Ecthyma gangrenosum is Pseudomonas vasculitis of skin in neutropenic or septicaemic patients with black necrotic centres.
r: Incorrect. That gives coral-red fluorescence of erythrasma.
Correct. Black necrotic ulcer in neutropenia.
Incorrect. That gives honey crusts or boils.
Incorrect. That gives erysipelas or scarlet fever.
items.kp: Black haloed ulcer in neutropenia is Pseudomonas.

items.q: A child with sore throat develops diffuse sandpaper rash, Pastia lines in flexures and a strawberry tongue. The cause is?
items.exp: Scarlet fever follows streptococcal pharyngitis with erythrogenic toxin rash, Pastia lines and strawberry tongue.
r: Correct. Sandpaper plus Pastia lines is scarlatinal.
Incorrect. That causes scalded skin peeling.
Incorrect. That is a cell-wall component, not the rash toxin.
Incorrect. That causes haemolytic uraemic syndrome.
items.kp: Sandpaper rash after sore throat is scarlet fever.

items.q: Limited impetigo with a few crusted spots and no systemic features is best managed initially with?
o: Topical antistaphylococcal ointment with hygiene measures
items.exp: Small localised impetigo responds to topical antibiotics with crust removal and hygiene; extensive or systemic disease needs oral agents.
r: Incorrect. Steroids worsen bacterial infection.
Incorrect. Antifungals do not cover cocci.
Incorrect. Retinoids treat acne, not infection.
Correct. Limited disease needs topical therapy.

items.q: A sweaty athlete has pitted punched-out erosions with foul odour on weight-bearing soles. Wood lamp and cause are?
o: Yellow fluorescence from Malassezia in versicolor
No fluorescence from Trichophyton in moccasin tinea
Coral-red fluorescence from Corynebacterium in pitted keratolysis
Green fluorescence from Microsporum in tinea pedis
items.exp: Pitted keratolysis is a Corynebacterium infection of plantar stratum corneum with pits, odour and coral-red Wood fluorescence.
r: Incorrect. Versicolor affects trunk, not pitted soles.
Incorrect. Moccasin tinea is diffuse scaling.
Correct. Pits plus odour plus coral-red glow.
Incorrect. Tinea pedis shows scaling, not pits.
items.kp: Smelly pitted soles mean pitted keratolysis.
